title: Go SDK: harden streaming reader for partial SSE frames + disconnects; deterministic shutdown on context cancel
author: Mateusz Zielinski
description:
Context: We’ve seen a few failure modes in streaming (SSE) where the Go client either (a) fails to parse events when proxies split frames across TCP reads, (b) returns opaque errors on mid-stream disconnects, or (c) hangs during shutdown because the read loop doesn’t deterministically exit when the caller cancels the context. This PR hardens the streaming reader implementation to be robust to partial reads and to guarantee bounded shutdown behavior on ctx cancel. This is part of the cross-SDK streaming parity work (ENG-2483) and aligns behavior with the draft disconnect handling policy.

What changed: (1) Replace the previous line-oriented scan loop with a buffered reader + incremental SSE parser that can handle partial lines/frames across reads. We now accumulate bytes until a full "\n\n" event boundary is observed (with support for CRLF), then parse "event:", "data:", "id:", and comments per SSE rules. (2) Ensure deterministic shutdown: the stream reader now owns a single goroutine responsible for IO reads and event parsing; ctx cancellation triggers an immediate Close on the response body and unblocks the read loop. We use an errgroup + a bounded channel to prevent goroutine leaks when downstream consumers stop reading. (3) Improve disconnect classification: io.EOF and net errors after at least one well-formed event are surfaced as StreamDisconnectedError with metadata (bytes_read, events_seen, last_event_id when present). Disconnects before the first event remain a transport error (retryable at higher layer). (4) Tighten cancellation semantics: if ctx is canceled, the iterator returns context.Canceled (wrapped as SDK error type for consistency) and does not emit a final partial event. (5) Add tests + fixtures: new table-driven tests cover partial frame splits, CRLF handling, large data lines, proxy-buffer-like chunking, and cancellation while blocked on Read.

Why this approach: bufio.Scanner has token limits and assumes newline-delimited tokens; SSE framing is "\n\n" delimited and can legally contain multiple data lines per event, and proxies commonly chunk mid-line. The incremental parser approach is more correct and matches what we want across SDKs (be permissive in parsing, strict in emitting complete events).

Testing: Added unit tests in streaming_reader_test.go (including a fake net.Conn that splits reads deterministically), plus an integration-ish test using httptest.Server that simulates a server writing partial frames with delays. Ran: go test ./... and go test -race ./... locally. CI includes race + vet.

Notes for follow-ups: This PR intentionally does not implement automatic reconnect/resume. Per ENG-2483 / ADR-0138 direction, we surface disconnects predictably and allow higher layers to decide whether a request is safe to retry. We should wire these scenarios into the conformance harness once the shared fixtures land (ENG-2485).
commits: streaming: replace scanner loop with incremental SSE parser
streaming: close response body on ctx cancel to unblock reads
tests: add partial frame + CRLF + cancel coverage
docs: update streaming godoc for disconnect/cancel semantics
changed_areas: README (Go SDK streaming section - small wording update)
conversation: Ibrahim Khan (review): Can we confirm we don’t leak goroutines if the user stops ranging over events? I’m worried about the producer blocking on send.

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Good call. I switched the event channel to be bounded and added a drain-on-close path. Also, ctx cancel now closes body which unblocks the producer; added a test that stops consuming after N events and asserts goroutine count stays stable under -race.
Rafael Mendes (review): Please ensure cancel exits fast even if server is stuck and TCP doesn’t close. Closing the body should do it, but add a deadline in tests so we don’t reintroduce hangs.
Mateusz Zielinski (author): Added a cancellation test with a 250ms budget and a fake reader that blocks until Close is called. The test fails if we don’t exit in time.
Amara Diallo (review): For disconnect classification, do we want to treat EOF after first event as a distinct error? Gateway sometimes closes idle streams; consistent error type will help support.

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Yes—now StreamDisconnectedError when we’ve seen >=1 full event, else it’s a transport error. This matches the current draft policy for surfacing mid-stream drops without pretending it’s retryable by default.
Tomáš Novák (review): Minor: record last_event_id only when present; otherwise keep empty string. Also, please include bytes_read for debugging.
Mateusz Zielinski (author): Done. StreamDisconnectedError now includes BytesRead and LastEventID (optional) and we populate it in both EOF and net.Error paths.
release_notes: Go SDK streaming: Improved SSE parsing robustness for partial frames/CRLF, deterministic shutdown on context cancellation, and clearer mid-stream disconnect errors.
